h1:
Phrae Old Town Cafes
10 Quiet Wooden-House Coffee Spots
intro: Phrae's charm is the old teak houses standing all over town. Turn one into a cafe and you get an atmosphere that's hard to find anywhere else — a cup of coffee inside a century-old wooden house, with a cool breeze through the old window shutters. We walked the Nai Wiang quarter around Wat Phong Sunan and Kham Lue Road, then picked 10 spots that are genuinely quiet and where locals actually sit, not just photo corners.

blocks.html: Phrae is a town you can wander slowly all day. The old teak houses are still standing across whole streets, and many have been turned into cafes that kept the original frame, wooden floors, and window shutters — giving a feel that a cafe in a new building just can't match. The other plus is that the town still isn't crowded. On a weekday, walk into almost any spot and you'll usually find a quiet corner to settle in for a while.

We ranked these on three things: the building has to be a real wooden or old house, not just wood-look decor; quiet enough to sip a coffee and read; and in or near the old town, a short walk or drive from one another. The prices we list are rough ranges from the drink menus and may shift with the season.

blocks.text: 10 Phrae old town cafes in wooden and old houses

items.name: Slope Coffee (Baan Bew)
items.blurb: A cafe in a wooden house over a hundred years old that leans slightly, earning it the nickname Baan Bew ("the crooked house"). Inside it's full of retro pieces from the '80s and '90s, so sitting here feels like having coffee at a relative's place — quiet and warm. It's the spot Phrae locals think of first when wooden-house cafes come up.
items.meta: Kham Lue Road, near Wat Phong Sunan · open 08:00–18:00

items.name: Le Gong Kao (Café de PhraeRis)
items.blurb: A classic two-storey wooden house standing tall on Kham Lue Road, done in a light Lanna-meets-modern style with the whole timber frame kept intact. The upstairs is a quiet corner you can sit in for a while, and the coffee is taken seriously. The orders people make most are the affogato and the macadamia cheesecake.
items.meta: Kham Lue Road, Nai Wiang · open 08:00–17:00

items.name: Je Bar Coffee & Pastry
items.blurb: A wooden house with a slightly modern touch, with both indoor and outdoor seating, in an old-temple quarter that's nice to stroll. The draw is the bakery, baked fresh daily — croissants, garlic butter bread, cheese bread — paired with an iced latte. Prices are easy, making it a good break between walks around the old town.
items.meta: Kham Lue Road, Wat Phong Sunan area · open 08:00–17:00

items.name: Ho: BAKE & CRAFT CAFE'
items.blurb: A cafe under the raised floor of a traditional wooden house, fitted out with wooden furniture and old pieces for a Thai vintage feel, among shady trees. It's a quiet spot, good for working or reading, with homemade bakery to go with the coffee.
items.meta: In Phrae town, near the old quarter · open roughly 09:00–17:00

items.name: On The FENCE
items.blurb: A small cafe in an old wooden house renovated in a homey minimalist style. The space isn't big but the seating corners are nicely set, and it doesn't get packed — good for anyone who wants real quiet to sip a coffee alone or as a pair.

items.name: SCENT Urban Coffee
items.blurb: A single-unit wooden shophouse in the Kad Nam Thong area, focused seriously on specialty coffee — the owner roasts in-house and has won awards. Worth trying are the single-origin iced americano and the matcha latte. The space is small and quiet, suited to coffee people who want to drink while focusing on the flavor.
items.meta: Kad Nam Thong area, in town · check opening hours on their page before you go

items.name: Charlotte Hut Coffee & Tea Bar
items.blurb: A European-vintage style house in a garden, with both indoor seating and tables out among the greenery — a homey, warm feel. The standouts are the orange espresso and the almond cake. Good for a long sit from late morning into the afternoon when the sun isn't harsh.

items.name: Sugar Bites Café & Homemade Bakery
items.blurb: A homemade-bakery cafe with both a garden zone and an air-conditioned room, recently expanded for more comfortable seating. The feel is friendly, like a cafe in your own neighborhood — good for anyone who likes baked goods with their coffee. The cappuccino comes out nicely smooth.

items.name: Teak Wood Cafe
items.blurb: A two-storey teak cafe — the house and the tables are made from teak the owner has collected over decades. Lots of seating, plenty of parking, over in Den Chai district. It's a bit of a drive out of the old town, but worth it if you like genuine teak craft. The signature is the Teak Wood drink, mixing kiwi, lemon and soda with coffee.
items.meta: Den Chai district (about 25–30 min drive from the old town) · open 08:00–17:00

items.name: Old wooden-house cafes along the Nai Wiang lanes
items.blurb: Down the lanes of the old quarter there are still several small wooden-house cafes that aren't famous but have a good feel, opening and closing on the owner's whim. If you're strolling the Kham Lue–Phong Sunan area and spot a wooden house open, drop in — you'll often find a quiet corner the crowds haven't reached.
items.meta: Lanes of the Nai Wiang quarter, around Wat Phong Sunan–Khum Chao Luang · hours vary by shop

blocks.title: When it's least crowded
blocks.html: Most Phrae cafes open early, around 8–9am. The quietest windows are before 11am and in the late afternoon, around 3–4pm. Weekdays are much quieter than weekends. If you want a long corner to read in, avoid the noon-to-2pm stretch on days off.

blocks.text: How to cafe-hop the Nai Wiang quarter well

blocks.html: The good thing about Phrae is that many of the standout cafes cluster along Kham Lue Road and around Wat Phong Sunan, all within walking distance. Park once and you can tick off several spots in one morning. Along the way you'll also pass old wooden houses, Khum Chao Luang, and Wong Buri House to stop for photos and soak up the old-town feel as you go.

items: Start early — wooden-house spots like Slope Coffee or Le Gong Kao open at 8am; go then for nice light and fewer people.
Late morning to noon — drop by Je Bar for fresh-baked bakery, then wander the old-temple quarter around it.
Afternoon — finish at SCENT Urban Coffee or Charlotte Hut for a long sit while the sun softens.
If you have time left — drive out to Teak Wood Cafe in Den Chai if you want to see a whole house of real teak.

blocks.text: Out-of-town cafes a short drive away

blocks.html: If you're in Phrae for a few days and want a change from the wooden houses in town, the area around it still has field-view cafes and teak cafes a short drive away — good for a day when you want to sit outdoors and catch a cool breeze.

items.name: Teak Wood Cafe (Den Chai)
items.blurb: A genuine two-storey teak house with lots of seating and plenty of parking, about a 25–30 min drive from the old town — good for anyone who likes teak craft.

items.name: Field-view cafes around town
items.blurb: Phrae's outskirts have several cafes set among fields and by the water, good for sitting outdoors in the cool of the morning or evening.

faq.q: Which wooden-house cafe in Phrae's old town is the best?
faq.a: Judged on real wooden-house atmosphere and quiet, Slope Coffee — also known as Baan Bew — comes near the top, since it's a genuine house over a hundred years old. Next is Le Gong Kao, a two-storey wooden house on Kham Lue Road. Both are in the Nai Wiang quarter, within walking distance of each other.

faq.q: Which area are most of Phrae's old town cafes in?
faq.a: They cluster along Kham Lue Road and around Wat Phong Sunan in the Nai Wiang quarter, with several within walking distance of one another, close to Khum Chao Luang and Wong Buri House. That makes it easy to cafe-hop and visit the old wooden houses in the same trip.

faq.q: How much does coffee cost at Phrae cafes?
faq.a: Most run ฿45–85 a cup. Bakery spots like Je Bar or Sugar Bites start around ฿45–65, while a specialty coffee shop like SCENT goes a touch higher depending on the bean grade. On the whole it's easier on the wallet than cafes in the big cities.

faq.q: When is the least crowded time to go to Phrae cafes?
faq.a: Weekdays before 11am and from 3–4pm are quietest. On weekends, noon to 2pm gets busy. If you want a long, peaceful sit, it's best to avoid that window.

faq.q: Can you visit Phrae's old town cafes without your own car?
faq.a: Yes — the standout cafes in Nai Wiang are within walking distance, so park once or rent a bicycle/motorbike in town and you can hit several in one morning. For out-of-town spots like Teak Wood, use a rental car or taxi only on a day you want to head further out.
